name: Exhaust
why: Makes the engine sound a lot better. Probably the most common mod people do on a Beat.
tip: Some are race-only and really loud, so read the description.

name: Air intake / filter
why: Cheap and easy. Adds some sound but not much power.
tip: Even if you keep the stock setup, a new filter is only about $15 to $35.

name: Coilovers
why: Replaces the old shocks. You can adjust how low it sits and how stiff it is.
tip: Don't go too low. Get an alignment after.

name: Strut tower bars
why: Bolts across the strut towers and makes the body stiffer. Helps a lot on a convertible.
tip: The price is for one bar. There's a front one and a rear one.

name: Tires
why: New tires make the biggest difference for the money.
tip: Sizes are 155/65R13 front and 165/60R14 rear. The date code on the sidewall tells you how old they are.

name: Brake pads + rotors
why: Better pads and rotors so it stops better.
tip: A set of pads is about $60. Only do rotors if the old ones are worn.

name: Roll bar
why: Safer if the car ever flips, and it makes the chassis stiffer.
tip: Most street cars use the rear 4-point one.

name: Vinyl wrap
why: Changes the color without paint, and it peels off later. You can do the whole car or just the roof, hood or mirrors.
tip: The low end is doing it yourself, the high end is a shop doing the whole car. The Beat is tiny so it needs a lot less film than a normal car.

name: Stickers + decals
why: Easiest way to make it yours. Small stickers on the rear window or bumper, or the Honda side decals some Beats came with.
tip: Clean the spot with rubbing alcohol first so they stay on.

name: Window tint
why: Keeps the inside cooler and makes the car look cleaner.
tip: Every state has its own limit on how dark the front windows can be, so ask the tint shop. They usually won't do the plastic rear window on the soft top.

name: Underglow
why: LED strips under the car. It can glow pink.
tip: Some states don't allow certain colors or having it on while driving. Fine for parked at meets.

name: Red H badge
why: Swap the chrome Honda H for a red one like a Type R has.
tip: Measure the old badge first, they come in a few sizes.

name: Tow strap
why: A bright fabric tow strap on the front bumper. Mostly for looks.
tip: They make them in pink. Check how it mounts first, some need a tow hook point.

name: Valve stem caps
why: Tiny colored caps for the tire valves. Looks cute against white wheels.
tip: Aluminum ones can get stuck if left on for years. A little grease on the threads helps.

name: License plate frame
why: Easy way to add some pink to the back of the car.
tip: Check how your plate is mounted first. The Beat bumper was made for a smaller Japanese plate.

name: Front lip / rear spoiler
why: Front lip, rear spoiler, or a full kit.
tip: Most of these come unpainted, so they need to be painted to match.

name: LED bulbs
why: White LEDs for the parking lights, license plate light, and reverse lights.
tip: Easiest one on the list.

name: Headlights + taillights
why: Old headlight lenses get yellow and cloudy. New ones make the whole car look newer.
tip: If they're only a little cloudy, a $20 restore kit from an auto parts store might be enough.

name: Hardtop
why: Good for winter and it's quieter on the highway.
tip: These don't come up often in the US, so grab one if you see it.

name: Interior LED lights
why: Soft light in the footwells at night. They come in pink.
tip: The USB or 12V plug-in ones don't need any wiring.

name: Seat covers
why: Protects the original zebra seats, which are really hard to replace.
tip: The Beat seats are small, so check the measurements before buying.

name: Shift knob
why: Easy swap that you touch every time you drive.
tip: Hondas use an M10x1.5 thread, so most Honda shift knobs screw right on.

name: Omamori charm
why: A Japanese good luck charm from a shrine. The traffic safety ones are made to hang in a car.
tip: Hang it from the mirror or tuck it somewhere it won't swing into the windshield.

name: Steering wheel + hub
why: Aftermarket steering wheel. Needs a hub adapter to fit.
tip: The hub is cheap ($15 to $45). Used Nardi and Momo wheels are easy to find.

name: Seats + rails
why: Rails for a bucket seat. Sits you lower and holds you in better.
tip: The price is just the rails, the seat is separate. Keep the stock zebra seats though.

name: Floor mats
why: Cheap and makes the inside look new. They come in red and checkered.
tip: Get ones made for the Beat. Generic mats slide under the pedals.

name: Hello Kitty decals
why: Hello Kitty stickers and vinyl decals. Small ones on the windows or a bigger one down the side. Hello Kitty is basically a cat, so it fits.
tip: Vinyl decals hold up to sun and car washes way better than paper stickers.

name: Hello Kitty steering wheel cover
why: Pink Hello Kitty cover for the steering wheel. Soft and cute.
tip: Measure across the wheel first. Most covers are made for a 15 inch wheel.

name: Hello Kitty seat + headrest covers
why: Hello Kitty covers for the seats or just the headrests. Also keeps the zebra seats safe.
tip: The Beat seats are small, so full covers might not fit right. Check the measurements.

name: Hello Kitty plushie + little stuff
why: A Hello Kitty plush for the dash or passenger seat, plus the little stuff like a tissue box cover, coasters or an air freshener.
tip: Keep anything on the dash small and stuck down so it doesn't fly around in a corner.

name: Kuromi, My Melody + friends
why: The rest of the Sanrio gang. Kuromi is the pink and black one, a little goth. They all come as decals, plushies and covers.
tip: Kuromi's pink and black would go with the dark soft top.

name: Rilakkuma stuff
why: The lazy bear. In Japan there's a ton of Rilakkuma car stuff: seat belt pads, tissue box covers, headrest covers, little plushies.
tip: The ones dressed up as cats exist too.

name: Miffy stuff
why: Simple little Miffy decals or a plush on the dash. Cute without being a lot.
tip: A small Miffy sticker in the corner of the back window would be perfect.

name: Fuzzy dice
why: Fuzzy dice for the mirror. Retro and a little silly.
tip: Hang them short so they don't swing into the windshield.

name: Mirror charm
why: Something cute hanging from the rearview mirror. A beaded charm, a little plush, or a crystal that makes rainbows when the sun hits it.
tip: Keep it small. Some states don't allow big things hanging from the mirror.

name: Air fresheners + vent clips
why: Cute air fresheners like strawberries, flowers or little cats, and clip-on vent decorations like daisies.
tip: Vent clips are easier than hanging ones in a car this small.

name: Flower + sakura decals
why: Daisy, hibiscus or cherry blossom vinyl decals down the side or on the hood.
tip: White and light pink flowers would really stand out on the red.

name: Colored lug nuts
why: Colored lug nuts. Pink, black or gold would all pop against the white wheels.
tip: Hondas use M12x1.5 lug nuts. You need 16, and they have to match the seat type of the wheels.

name: Painted brake calipers
why: Paint the brake calipers. You'd see them through the spokes of the white wheels.
tip: Use real caliper paint since it handles the heat. It's a weekend job: wheels off, clean, tape, paint.

name: Dashboard cat
why: A cat for the dashboard.
tip: The solar ones nod their head while you drive. Museum putty keeps it from sliding.

name: Stickers of Ahna and Blu
why: Custom stickers made from photos of Ahna and Blu. Lots of shops do this, you just send them a picture.
tip: Ask for outdoor vinyl if it's going on the car, regular stickers fade.

name: Black cat decal
why: A little black cat sticker that looks like Ahna. The ones that look like they're peeking over an edge are cute on the trunk.
tip: Black vinyl shows up best on the red paint.

name: Cat ears
why: Little cat ears that stick onto the car.
tip: They won't stick to the soft top fabric, so they'd go on the trunk lid or a hardtop.

name: Paw print decals
why: Little paw prints walking across the hood or up the side.
tip: Vinyl decals peel off clean later if you change your mind.

name: Cat seat belt pads
why: Plush cat covers for the seat belts. Comfy and cute.
tip: The shoulder pad kind wraps around the belt with velcro.

name: Timing belt + water pump
why: If there's no record of it being done, it should be done before anything else.
tip: The bigger kits come with the water pump and tensioner. Labor usually costs more than the parts.

name: Radiator + cooling
why: The radiator is in the front and the engine is in the middle, so cooling is a known weak spot.
tip: A new radiator cap is about $25 and worth doing either way.

name: Soft top
why: The plastic rear window gets cloudy and the seals leak as they get old.
tip: Yours looks fine in the pictures, so this is for later.

name: Clutch
why: Only needed when it starts slipping. Just good to know the price.
tip: A full clutch job means the engine comes out the bottom, so it's a shop job. The cylinder rebuild kits are easier.
